summary: Hermann Berger worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under doctoral and habilitation supervisor Helmut Hoffmann around 1950 to 1956, and held a post at the University of Heidelberg in 1965.
Hermann Beythan worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

Hermann Bonitz was a scholar of philosophy and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Leipzig (~1832-1834) and Berlin (~1834-1836), and later held posts at the University of Vienna (~1849-1867) and the Prussian Ministry of Spiritual, Educational and Medical Affairs (~1875-1888).

Hermann Brockhaus worked in Indology and linguistics, having studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn, including under August Wilhelm von Schlegel (~1828-1830). He served as professor at the University of Jena (1839) and the University of Leipzig (1848, 1872-1877).

Hermann Brunnhofer studied at Bonn, Berlin (under Albrecht Weber ~1866-1868), and Zurich. He held positions at Kuldīga Gymnasium (~1875-1881), Oxford (~1883-1885), Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek (~1885-1888), Saint Petersburg (1891-1901), and the University of Bern (1901-1914).
Hermann Camillo Kellner specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1864-1868) and served as Gymnasialprofessor at Königliches Gymnasium Zwickau (~1875-1902).

Hermann Collitz worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Göttingen, Halle, and Berlin under August Fick, Theodor Benfey, Hermann Sauppe, and Adalbert Bezzenberger. He taught at Bryn Mawr College (1885-1907) and held a chair at Johns Hopkins University (1907-1928).
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1876-1880). He served as professor of mathematics at the University of Giessen (~1899-1922).

Hermann Goetz studied at the University of Munich (~1920-1923) and under Jean Philippe Vogel (~1931-1936). He held posts at the Baroda Museum (1939-1953), National Gallery of Modern Art (~1953-1955), and the University of Heidelberg (1961-1976).
Hermann Güntert worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1921-1923) and the University of Heidelberg (~1923-1945).

Hermann Günther Grassmann worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Berlin (1827-1830) under Friedrich Schleiermacher, and later taught at schools in Berlin and Stettin, including the Marienstiftsgymnasium (1832-1834, 1852-1877).

Hermann Hirt worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Leipzig, later serving as Privatdozent at Leipzig (1891-1912) and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at the University of Giessen (1912-1936).

Hermann Hunger worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Vienna, Heidelberg, and Münster, and later held positions at the University of Chicago (~1967-1970), German Archaeological Institute (~1970-1973), and University of Vienna (~1978-2007).

Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Bonn under Johann Gildemeister. He served as professor at the University of Münster (1876-1885), Kiel University (1885), and the University of Bonn (1889-1922).

Hermann Kulke worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Freiburg, Madras, and Heidelberg, studying under Hermann Goetz. He held academic posts at the University of Heidelberg (1967-1988) and served as Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988-2003).

Hermann Oldenberg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen and Berlin. He served as professor at the University of Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889, 1898; Rektor 1906-1907), and the University of Göttingen (1908).

Hermann Osthoff worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn under Hermann Usener, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held posts at the University of Leipzig (~1875-1877) and as Ordinarius at the University of Heidelberg (1877).

Hermann Sauppe worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He completed his doctorate under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig (~1827-1832) and held academic posts at the University of Zurich (1833, 1838) and the University of Göttingen (1855).
Hermann Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich (~1844-1848) and later held a post at the University of Berlin (~1853-1854).

Hermann Usener worked in religious studies, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn (~1852-1857), holding posts at the University of Bern (~1861-1863), University of Greifswald (~1863-1866), and University of Bonn (~1866-1905).
